note: Hebrew ha'almah is "the young woman" (of marriageable age; the specific word for virgin is betulah), and harah is an adjective, "pregnant" (now or about to be). The KJV follows the LXX parthenos, the reading Matthew 1:23 quotes. Theologically the most debated verse in Isaiah. Context: the young woman is pregnant (a sign in Ahaz's time) (medium confidence). 'Almah is a young woman of marriageable age (Gen 24:43; Exod 2:8), not the specific word for virgin (betulah); Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion render neanis. Harah is an adjective, 'pregnant', and v. 16 sets the sign within a few years. But harah can look forward (Judg 13:5), and the major versions divide, so this is favoured rather than certain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'the/a virgin shall conceive' — LXX parthenos, Vulgate virgo, Matt 1:23, KJV, ESV, NIV, NASB, CSB, holding that 'almah implies an unmarried, chaste girl and that the sign looks to the Messiah; (2) 'the young woman shall conceive / is about to conceive' (future) — RSV, NET; (3) the mother identified as Ahaz's wife or Isaiah's wife (cf. 8:3) — Jewish tradition and many commentators.
